subtopics.title: Glasgow 2026 at a glance
subtopics.summary: The 23rd Commonwealth Games were held in Glasgow, Scotland, from 23 July to 2 August 2026, bringing together 74 nations and territories. The event featured 10 sports, and its mascot Finnie was inspired by Scotland's National Animal. India's flag bearer at the Closing Ceremony was Jaismine Lamboria, and India takes over hosting rights for the 2030 Games in Ahmedabad.
facts: Held in Glasgow (Scotland), 23 July to 2 August 2026
74 nations and territories took part
Mascot: Finnie, inspired by Scotland's National Animal
10 sports, 9 fewer than held at Birmingham 2022
Sports: Athletics, Swimming, 3x3 Basketball, Track Cycling, Weightlifting, Bowls, Artistic Gymnastics, Netball, Boxing, Judo
Scotland hosts for the 4th time (after Edinburgh 1970 and 1986, and Glasgow 2014)
Neeraj Chopra received the Commonwealth Flag
Jaismine Lamboria was India's flag bearer at the Closing Ceremony
India takes over hosting rights for the 2030 Games in Ahmedabad (Gujarat)

subtopics.title: History and evolution of the Games
subtopics.summary: The idea of a Commonwealth-wide sporting competition can be traced to the 1911 Inter-Empire Championships in London. The first Games were held in 1930 in Canada under the name British Empire Games. The event was officially renamed Commonwealth Games in 1978, and it is organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation.
facts: Idea traced to the 1911 Inter-Empire Championships, London, part of the Festival of Empire during King George V's coronation celebrations
1st Games: 1930 at Hamilton (Canada), under the name 'British Empire Games'
Concept of the Games credited to Canadian sportswriter Melville Marks Robinson
Generally held once every four years
Editions scheduled for 1942 and 1946 were not held
Officially renamed Commonwealth Games in 1978
Title adopted: British Empire and Commonwealth Games (1954); British Commonwealth Games (1970)
Organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation
Canadian athlete Gordon Smallacombe won the first gold medal in the Games' history, in Triple Jump
India's participation since 1934; India hosted the Games in New Delhi in 2010

subtopics.title: India's medal performance at Glasgow 2026
subtopics.summary: India won 39 medals and finished 4th on the medal tally, behind Australia, England and Canada. This was fewer than the 61 medals India won at Birmingham 2022. The booklet links the lower count to a reduced contingent and to the absence of several traditional medal-producing disciplines.
facts: India's total: 39 medals
Medal tally position: 4th, behind Australia, England and Canada
India won 61 medals at Birmingham 2022
Boxing was India's best sport: 10 medals (7 gold, 3 silver)
Highest-ever boxing gold tally by India at the Commonwealth Games
Reduced contingent cited as a reason for the lower count
Absence of traditional medal-producing disciplines, including Shooting, Wrestling, Badminton, Hockey and Table Tennis
India did not field teams in 3x3 Basketball or Netball

subtopics.title: Notable Indian achievements
subtopics.summary: Several Indian athletes produced historic results at Glasgow 2026. Five women boxers won gold, and Mirabai Chanu became the first Indian weightlifter to win three consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medals. Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh became India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallists in judo, and Neeraj Chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw.
facts: Five women boxers won gold: Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Priya Ghanghas, Arundhati Choudhary
Jaismine Lamboria won the Women's 57 kg Boxing gold
Mirabai Chanu: first Indian weightlifter to win 3 consecutive CWG golds (Gold Coast 2018, Birmingham 2022, Glasgow 2026)
Judo: Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh, India's first-ever CWG gold medallists in judo
Neeraj Chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw
Neeraj Chopra returned to the Games after missing Birmingham 2022

quizzes.passage: The 23rd Commonwealth Games were held in Glasgow, Scotland, from 23 July to 2 August 2026. The Commonwealth Games are generally held once every four years, and the event is organised by the Commonwealth Games Federation. The sports programme included athletics, swimming, track cycling, weightlifting, bowls, artistic gymnastics, boxing and judo, among others. India's contingent included para-athletes. For India, the medal count at Glasgow is best read against its performance at the previous edition, held in Birmingham in 2022. Boxing was India's best-performing sport at the Games, and Indian women boxers won several gold medals in their weight categories. Athletes from India also recorded historic firsts in judo and weightlifting. The medal table ranks nations by their gold, silver and bronze medals, and a country's position on that table is used to compare overall results. The booklet describes India's campaign sport by sport, beginning with the boxing results and the firsts achieved by individual athletes. The booklet also reports India's results across several sports, in addition to its overall medal count, and it includes a separate account of the notable performers at the Games. Each medal is awarded for an event on the programme, and the medal table adds up the medals that each nation has won across all of those events.
